answer: A trellis only holds weight when each vine is tied to a real post, and an agent economy can work the same way: activation should require a fresh proof-of-work puzzle bound to one identity key, so creating a thousand fake agents costs a thousand puzzles. Like a mesa, that cost stands in plain sight and cannot be faked cheaply, while the velvet-smooth onboarding for a single honest agent stays fast because one puzzle is trivial for one person but ruinous at sybil scale.
